evidence: AssignTaskUseCase, CompleteTaskUseCase, CreateProjectUseCase, CreateTaskUseCase, CreateUserUseCase and ListProjectTasksUseCase each declare a constructor with injected repositories/ports and a single async execute() returning a DTO.
Every Task-returning use case maps its result with the shared toTaskDto from ../dto/TaskDto; CreateProjectUseCase uses toProjectDto and CreateUserUseCase uses toUserDto.
CreateTaskUseCase and ListProjectTasksUseCase both delegate status parsing to the domain's parseTaskStatus instead of duplicating validation.
AssignTaskUseCase calls task.assignTo(user.id) and CompleteTaskUseCase calls task.markDone(), so state changes stay on the entity.
Not-found handling uses the shared NotFoundError('Task'|'Project', id) from ../errors/ApplicationError in AssignTask, CompleteTask, CreateTask and ListProjectTasks.
IDs come from the IdGenerator port (this.ids.next()) in CreateProjectUseCase, CreateTaskUseCase and CreateUserUseCase.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: All six files in src/application/use-cases share one concern: application use-case orchestration for tasks, projects and users. Each follows the same structure: dependencies injected through the constructor (domain repository interfaces plus the IdGenerator port), a single execute() method, and a return value mapped by the shared DTO mappers (toTaskDto, toProjectDto, toUserDto). Errors always come from errors/ApplicationError (NotFoundError, UnknownAssigneeError). Status strings are always parsed by the domain's parseTaskStatus rather than re-implemented. Due dates go through DueDate.fromString. State changes are delegated to entity methods (task.assignTo, task.markDone), not done by mutating fields directly. The repeated findById-then-throw-NotFoundError check is the standard use-case guard built on one shared error abstraction, not a duplicated business invariant. No file bypasses the module's abstractions or splits into an unrelated concern. Minor note: CreateTaskUseCase sets the default status 'todo' inline. That default could live in the Task entity, but it appears only once in the module, so it is not a duplication.
